title: All six identity fields
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Refused requests are not logged. Gateway denials for bad logins have 'unknown' in their identity fields.
steps: 1. Open `src/gateway.py` line 132. Fill the unknown fields from the caller's certificate and mark the row `untrusted_caller`. 2. Open `src/main.py` line 114. Before returning 401, write an audit row with all six fields set to the string `untrusted_caller`. 3. If that write fails, return 503 instead of 401. 4. Create a test that sends a bad token. Check an audit row exists.
done_when: A request with a bad token creates an audit row in both the agent and the gateway.

title: Content-derived type identity
priority: Must fix before release

Add a loop to the test that changes one input at a time and checks the id changes each time. 4. Run the test in `.github/workflows/release.yml` before line 45.
done_when: Changing any input file, the model record or the digest changes the agent-type-id.

title: Trustworthy attribution
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The gateway trusts a caller header for the instance, and a resumed run starts a new trace.
steps: 1. Open `src/gateway.py` line 170. Replace the header with a verified value from the token, such as a new `inst` claim set by the STS. 2. Open `src/main.py` line 147. Store the trace parent with the approval grant and restore it on resume. 3. Create a test that sends a forged `X-Agent-Instance`. Check that the gateway ignores it.
done_when: The gateway uses an instance id from the signed token, and a resumed run continues the original trace.

title: Operational lookup

Replace the header values with ids from the verified token. 3. Create a stop flag for one agent type in a test cluster. Check that the gateway refuses that type only.

priority: Show proof it works before release
problem: Branch protection is set in GitHub, not in the repository, so it cannot be checked from code.
steps: 1. Ask a repository admin to export the `main` branch ruleset from GitHub settings. 2. Check it blocks force-pushes and deletion, and needs review from the code owners in `CODEOWNERS`. 3. Save the export in the review record.
done_when: A saved ruleset shows force-pushes and deletion are blocked on `main`.

title: Environment isolation
priority: Show proof it works, or get a written risk approval
problem: Network rules look sound in the manifests, but nothing proves they work in the running cluster.
steps: 1. Ask the platform team to run a pod in `hr-agent` that tries `curl` to a public host, the cloud metadata address and a pod in another namespace. 2. Save the output. All three must fail. Only the hosts in `k8s/networkpolicy.yaml` lines 20 to 31 should work. 3. Attach the output to the review record.
done_when: A saved test run shows the pod cannot reach metadata endpoints or hosts outside the allowed list.

title: Minimal, isolated runtime
priority: Show proof it works, or get a written risk approval
problem: The audit job runs a platform image whose contents are not visible, so we cannot confirm it has no shell or downloader.
steps: 1. Ask the platform team for the SBOM of the psql image used on line 26 of `k8s/audit-maintenance.yaml`. 2. Check it for a shell, `curl`, `wget` and a package manager. 3. Save the result in the review record.
done_when: An SBOM for the psql image shows no shell, downloader or package manager.

title: Fleet incident response
priority: Show proof it works
problem: The repository has no incident runbook. It has no impact query and no owner for outside reports.
steps: 1. Ask the security team for the runbook for a bad tool server or vendor. 2. Run the drill. Keep the impact query, quarantine and revocation records, alert times and the name of the person who decides on outside reporting. 3. Note that the gateway stop query in `src/gateway.py` line 99 ignores the agent type.
done_when: A drill record shows the impact query, a quarantine and a named reporting decision-maker.

title: Security monitoring
priority: Show proof it works
problem: No security detection rules or alert routing are in the repository. They may exist elsewhere.
steps: 1. Ask the security team for the rules that alert on five events: denied calls, stops, approval failures, quota stops and audit failures. 2. Ask them to send a test alert. Record the time it reached the security responder. 3. Save the rules and the test result in the review record.
done_when: Saved rules and a timed test alert show the five event types reach a security responder.

title: Misaligned-behavior review
priority: Show proof it works
problem: Nothing reviews what the agent does. No one has said if a rogue agent is in scope.
steps: 1. Ask the security lead to decide whether a misaligned agent is in scope. Write the decision in `release/manifest.yaml`. 2. If it is in scope, add a second check that sees only the proposed action, not untrusted text. Build a set of labeled test runs. 3. Measure how many bad runs the check misses. Save the result in the review record.
done_when: A written scope decision exists, and if in scope, a measured miss rate is on file.
